headline: Pretrained sequence models extend across DNA, RNA and protein tasks, with limits on ligand and structure sensitivity
label: Sequence Foundation Model Reliability
summary: New DNA, RNA and protein foundation models are benchmarked on structure, variant and site prediction, while a MET kinase benchmark exposes ligand-invariant behavior.
synthesis: The common thread is pretraining sequence representations and adapting them to downstream prediction. In nucleic acids, structRFM uses 21M sequence-structure pairs, LIMBER combines self-attention with Mamba on 40.5M ncRNAs, and IsoAlign applies JEPA objectives to isoform-aware DNA-protein alignment. In proteins, PALM adds LoRA and a BiLSTM to ESM2, MaskNGly predicts N-glycosylation zero-shot from PLM embeddings, and PDLMs jointly model protein-DNA pairs. AtomLM-9b tokenizes all-atom geometry. The reliability signal is the MET kinase deep mutational scanning benchmark: across 11 inhibitors, models are largely ligand-invariant, so learned representations may not capture inhibitor-specific effects. The RNA-small molecule review similarly emphasizes evaluation across binding site, preference and pose tasks.
